title: Pool cleaning equipment: tools for the water, the walls and the floor
audience: Pool service technicians who select, use and maintain the hand and powered tools used on a pool
learningOutcomes: Name the pool-specific cleaning tools and state the job each one does
Choose a brush for a pool surface by the finish, following the manufacturer's guidance
Run a weekly cleaning sequence that moves debris towards the drain and removes it from the water
Recognise that housekeeping and hotel cleaning equipment in the textbook is out of scope for pool work

instruction.heading: The tools a pool service uses
instruction.body: The US start-up guide and the textbook both name the core pool tools: a pool vacuum with its head, pole and hose; a debris net or collector for leaves and insects; brushes for the walls; a test kit for pH and sanitiser; and the chemicals the plan allows. The skimmer and its basket are part of the circulation system and are covered in “Pool circulation system: components and how they connect”, and the vacuum method is in “Vacuuming, vacuum to waste and automated cleaners”. This lesson deals with the walls, the surfaces and the debris.

instruction.heading: Choosing a brush
instruction.body: The US guide suggests a firm brush for concrete, a softer one for fibreglass, tile and vinyl, and a metal-bristled brush only for heavy algae and never on vinyl. Those are US guide statements. The real rule is that the brush must suit the finish, and the manufacturer's finish guidance for the pool is the reference. Use a soft brush on any surface that scratches easily, and keep metal bristles away from liners and from any finish the manufacturer prohibits. Work a long-handled brush from the shallow end towards the deep end, overlapping each stroke, so the loosened dirt is carried to the main drain.

instruction.heading: Debris and daily checks
instruction.body: The guide advises lifting leaves and insects off the surface with a collector, every day where trees overhang, and using a cover where leaves fall heavily. The textbook adds that skimmer baskets and the filter must be checked, and that the pump ought to be looked at every day. A blocked filter clouds the water, so confirm that water moves freely through it, and clean or replace the filter once it does not. That point matches “Backwash triggers, rinse and chemical cleaning for the sand bed”.

instruction.heading: A workable weekly order
instruction.body: A practical weekly order is to brush the walls and the waterline, lift off floating debris, empty the baskets, vacuum the floor in overlapping passes, check the pump and filtration unit, and test the water as the plan requires. Use the same order every week so that nothing is missed. Record what was done and anything that needs attention.

instruction.heading: Hygiene and out-of-scope items
instruction.body: Clean each tool after use, dry it, and keep it away from chemicals. Where several pools are served, keep a separate brush and net for each, so organisms are not carried between them. Equipment hygiene is covered in “Surface cleaning and equipment hygiene”. The textbook's housekeeping section lists mops, dustpans, carpet machines, vapour cleaners, laundry equipment and hotel trolleys. Those items are outside pool work and are not used here, and neither is a lawn scarifier.

procedure: Select the tools for the pool's finish, and check the brush suits the surface.
Brush the walls and waterline from the shallow end to the deep end, in overlapping strokes, moving debris to the drain.
Remove floating leaves and insects with the collector.
Empty the skimmer and the pump baskets and check the filter flow.
Vacuum the floor in overlapping passes at a steady pace.
Clean and dry the tools, and store them away from chemicals.
Record the tasks done and any defect found.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks you to use a steel brush to remove algae from a vinyl-lined pool because it works faster.
workedExamples.reasoning: Avoid using a steel brush on the vinyl. Use a brush that suits the liner and the finish guidance from the liner maker, and treat the algae with the plan's product. Record the request and the reason, and tell the customer that a damaged liner is costly to repair.

workedExamples.situation: The brush is worn and the bristles are splayed. The owner asks you to keep using it.
workedExamples.reasoning: Replace the brush. A worn brush does not clean and can scratch the surface. Record the condition, tell the owner, and refer the replacement.

equipmentAndPpe: Pool vacuum with head, pole and hose
Surface brush matched to the finish, with a soft option
Collector or net for floating debris
Test kit for pH and sanitiser

commonErrors.error: Using a brush that scratches the finish
commonErrors.prevention: Match the brush to the finish, using the manufacturer's guidance.

commonErrors.error: Brushing from the deep end upwards
commonErrors.prevention: Brush from the shallow end to the deep end so the dirt moves to the drain.

commonErrors.error: Using a worn brush or a damaged net
commonErrors.prevention: Replace worn or damaged tools, and record the replacement.

commonErrors.error: Using housekeeping equipment on the pool
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the pool-specific tools for the pool.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Keep the tools and the pole clear of overhead power lines and electrical equipment when working near the pool.
Do not run a powered tool near the water without a suitable residual current protection, and check the power supply for the tool.
Store tools away from chemicals, and keep brushes clean to avoid carrying contamination between pools.
Brush choice, finish guidance and tool suitability for a specific pool are set by the manufacturer.

qualityStandard: Each tool is matched to the pool finish, and any worn or damaged tool is replaced.
The weekly order is followed, and the tasks done are recorded.
Tools are cleaned, dried and stored separately from chemicals.
documentationEvidence: Weekly cleaning record with tasks done and defects
Referral note for filter flow or finish damage
summary: Match the brush to the finish and brush towards the drain.
Follow the same weekly order so that no task is missed.
Housekeeping equipment is out of scope for pool work.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which brush choice is correct for a fibreglass pool wall?
options: A steel brush, since it removes algae fastest and it is cheap to buy
A brush that suits the finish, with the manufacturer's guidance as the reference
A kitchen scrubbing pad and a bucket of hot pool water for the day
A wire brush from the workshop and a rusty old blade from the shed

knowledgeChecks.question: In which direction should a pool wall be brushed?
options: From the deep end upwards, against the drain and at a fast pace
Upward from the deep end, so that the debris floats to the skimmer
From the shallow end to the deep end, moving the debris to the drain
Only at the waterline and only on the side near the steps

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item is out of scope for pool cleaning work?
options: A pool vacuum head and its long hose
A test kit for pH and chlorine level
A skimmer net for floating debris
A hotel laundry or housekeeping trolley
